verses.pali: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā parittaṁ nakhasikhāyaṁ paṁsuṁ āropetvā bhikkhū āmantesi:
verses.english: Then the Buddha, picking up a little bit of dirt on his fingernail, addressed the mendicants:

verses.pali: katamaṁ nu kho bahutaraṁ, yo vāyaṁ mayā paritto nakhasikhāyaṁ paṁsu āropito, ayaṁ vā mahāpathavī”ti?
verses.english: Which is more: the little bit of dirt on my fingernail, or this great earth?”
“Sir, the great earth is far more.

verses.pali: Appamattako bhagavatā paritto nakhasikhāyaṁ paṁsu āropito.
verses.english: The little bit of dirt on your fingernail is tiny.

verses.pali: Neva satimaṁ kalaṁ upeti na sahassimaṁ kalaṁ upeti na satasahassimaṁ kalaṁ upeti mahāpathaviṁ upanidhāya bhagavatā paritto nakhasikhāyaṁ paṁsu āropito”ti.
verses.english: Compared to the great earth, it’s not nearly a hundredth, a thousandth, or a hundred thousandth part.”

verses.pali: “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa abhisametāvino etadeva bahutaraṁ dukkhaṁ yadidaṁ parikkhīṇaṁ pariyādiṇṇaṁ;
verses.english: “In the same way, for a noble disciple accomplished in view, an individual with comprehension, the suffering that’s over and done with is more,

verses.pali: Neva satimaṁ kalaṁ upeti na sahassimaṁ kalaṁ upeti na satasahassimaṁ kalaṁ upeti purimaṁ dukkhakkhandhaṁ parikkhīṇaṁ pariyādiṇṇaṁ upanidhāya yadidaṁ sattakkhattuṁparamatā.
verses.english: Compared to the mass of suffering in the past that’s over and done with, it’s not nearly a hundredth, a thousandth, or a hundred thousandth part, since there are at most seven more lives.
That’s how very beneficial it is to comprehend the teaching
and gain the vision of the teaching.”
